articles.title: Pre-term births in Bengal linked to heatwaves: Study - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Pre-term births in Bengal linked to heatwaves: Study
Bengal’s estimated excess rate of 11.9 per 1,000 births was close to Karnataka’s 12.2 and higher than Bihar’s 11.7. Nagaland recorded 11.8.
The analysis estimates that the April 2024 heatwave was associated with approximately 16,150 excess preterm births across India, Bangladesh and the Philippines compared with a typical April. In a separate assessment, researchers attributed around 10,600 additional preterm births across the three countries specifically to human-caused climate change.
India alone accounted for approximately 8,830 climate-attributable preterm births.
The findings carry particular significance for Bengal, where pregnant women face prolonged summer heat, high humidity and uneven access to cooling, especially in densely populated urban neighbourhoods and rural communities.
Joanne Bentley-McKune, lead author and senior research analyst at ZCA, said: “Climate change is making extreme heat more frequent and intense, raising the risk of preterm birth, which is linked to life-long health impacts.”
Rashmi Agarwalla, associate professor at AIIMS Guwahati, said anaemia, poor nutrition and prolonged outdoor work compound heat-related pregnancy risks, particularly among vulnerable communities. “Heat remains an often-overlooked threat to maternal and neonatal health,” she said.
The report calls for integrating heat protection into antenatal care, strengthening early-warning systems, improving access to cooling and preparing maternity services for increasing heat-related complications. For Bengal, the findings underline the need to treat extreme heat as a growing challenge to reproductive and public health.
